Hotline Miami

Dennaton Games’ 2012 top-down action game set in Miami in 1989: hot-pink and violet pixel art, wobbling magenta screens, and a soundtrack of synthwave artists.

Source
Steam: Hotline Miami
Creator
Dennaton Games (Jonatan Söderström and Dennis Wedin)
Made
Released 23 October 2012 (Wikipedia; Steam)
Styles
Synthwave (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person), Pixel Art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Violent, nocturnal, energetic
Evidence
Inspected a 1920 × 1080 gameplay screenshot and the 1920 × 620 library artwork from Steam in a scratch folder. Not stored.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: the game was released on Steam on 23 October 2012. Dennaton Games is “Swedish designer and programmer Jonatan Söderström and artist Dennis Wedin.” It is “Set in Miami in 1989.” Its graphics use “pixel art with a high-contrast colour palette.” Wikipedia.

Wikipedia: the film Drive (2011) inspired the creators, and the soundtrack “combines many music genres like electronic, techno, vaporwave, and synthwave”, with artists including M.O.O.N. and Perturbator.

The synthwave record names Hotline Miami among the works that spread the look.

Observed

  • The gameplay screenshot shows rooms from directly above in chunky pixel art: a pink rug, teal walls, cream sofas, and blood splatter.
  • The area outside the building is a flat hot-pink to magenta gradient, not black.
  • Scores such as “6501pts” and “+600PTS” are set in a wobbly, wide pixel script with a dark drop shadow, in cream, magenta, and teal.
  • The library artwork is a painted crowd of men in pale 1980s suits around a figure in a pig mask and a letterman jacket, under a dark violet night sky with lit windows and palm silhouettes.

Why it belongs

It belongs to the synthwave story more through sound, setting, and palette than through the Outrun scene. Its colours are the style’s magenta and teal, but they fill whole areas rather than glowing on black.

Borrow

Set score numbers in a wide, wobbling display face in magenta and teal on a dark plate.
